<p class="ltx_p">New coins <math id="S5.I5.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\textbf{c}^%
{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathcolor="#0000FF">c</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> are correctly derived from the old coins <math id="S5.I5.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}%
\textbf{c}^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathcolor="#BF0040">c</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S5.I5.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Blinded coins <math id="S5.I5.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%
\mathbf{c}}^{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">~</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> are correctly derived from <math id="S5.I5.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\textbf{c}^%
{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathcolor="#0000FF">c</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> and <math id="S5.I5.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[b_{j}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S5.I5.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Signatures <math id="S5.I5.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}%
\sigma^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">σ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> of the coin <math id="S5.I5.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}%
\mathbf{c}^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> are correct.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I5.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S5.I5.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Private addresses <math id="S5.I5.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}ask%
^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> match the public address <math id="S5.I5.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}apk%
^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I5.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">6.</span> 
<div id="S5.I5.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The sum of the values of the old coins <math id="S5.I5.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}%
\textbf{c}^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathcolor="#BF0040">c</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> equals the sum of the values of the new coins <math id="S5.I5.i6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\textbf{c}^%
{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathcolor="#0000FF">c</mtext><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="ltx_p">The user can now send the NIZK <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{transfer}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> along with the public inputs to all the validators. The detailed algorithm run by the validators is detailed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.
Once a validator receives the proof:</p>
<ol id="S5.I6" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S5.I6.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S5.I6.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It checks that none of the <math id="S5.I6.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}sn_%
{i}^{old}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> appears in its <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>;</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I6.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S5.I6.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">It checks that the proof <math id="S5.I6.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline"><mi>π</mi></math> is correct;</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I6.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S5.I6.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">If the last two conditions are fulfilled, it adds all <math id="S5.I6.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}sn_%
{i}^{old}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">n</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math> to <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>, add all <math id="S5.I6.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%
\mathbf{c}}^{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">~</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> to <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">signedCoinList</span>, it signs all the coins <math id="S5.I6.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%
\mathbf{c}}^{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">~</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> and returns the blinded partial signatures.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I6.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S5.I6.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">If any of the previous conditions is not fulfilled, the validator checks if the blinded coins <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%
\mathbf{c}}^{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">~</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> appear in <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">signedCoinList</span>.
If they all do, then the validator still sends back the signatures.
This is done because a Byzantine validator <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math> might receive a transfer request from a user <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> and send it to other validators using a private channel.
As a result, other validators might answer <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline"><mi>p</mi></math> before answering <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>, preventing <math id="S5.I6.i4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> from receiving the signatures while the old coins are actually spent (their serial numbers would have been added to <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span> already).</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="ltx_p">Once the user receives <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> valid partial signatures for the coins <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%
\mathbf{c}}^{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mo style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">~</mo></mover><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> from <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> validators, she can unblind and aggregate them to form <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m+1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> signatures <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\sigma_{j}}%
]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">σ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math> that are valid signatures for <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\mathbf{c}^%
{new}_{j}}]_{j=1}^{m+1}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></math>.
She can now send each couple <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\mathbf{c}^%
{new}_{j}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}%
\sigma^{new}_{j}})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">σ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}apk^{new}_{j}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math>.
The user <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}apk^{new}_{j}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow></math> only accepts the payment if <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\rho^{new}_{%
j}}\notin\mathsf{rhoList}_{{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{%
pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}apk^{new}_{j}}}" display="inline"><mrow><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">ρ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>∉</mo><msub><mi>𝗋𝗁𝗈𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx5.p2.m27" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathsf{VERIFY_{Sig}}({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{%
rgb}{0,0,1}\mathbf{c}^{new}_{j}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{%
pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\sigma^{new}_{j}},pk_{agg})==1" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>𝖵𝖤𝖱𝖨𝖥𝖸</mi><mi>𝖲𝗂𝗀</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">σ</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><msub><mi>k</mi><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>.<span id="footnote6" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">6</sup><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">6</span>For convenience, we allow the <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter ltx_font_smallcaps">Transfer</span> algorithm to send money to several recipients in a single call, in contrast with the specification, which allows only one recipient at a time.
As explained in the security proof in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>, this more generic transfer can be seen as a batch of successive transfer calls, each destined to a single user.</span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Double spending.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Consider a coin <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c}^{\text{old}}" display="inline"><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">𝐜</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">old</mtext></msup></math> that has been spent.
Hence, a set <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{1}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> of <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> validators have claimed to have added <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="sn^{\text{old}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">n</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">old</mtext></msup></mrow></math> to their <span class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>, and at least <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> out of them are correct.
If a Byzantine user tries to spend <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{c^{old}}" display="inline"><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">𝐨𝐥𝐝</mi></msup></math> again, it should collect confirmations from a set <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> of <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> validators that will have to add <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="sn^{\text{old}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">n</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">old</mtext></msup></mrow></math> in their <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span> again.
Since there are <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> validators in total, <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{1}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{2}" display="inline"><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> have at least one correct validator in common.
It must refuse to sign the second transaction because <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx6.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="sn^{\text{old}}" display="inline"><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">n</mi><mtext style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">old</mtext></msup></mrow></math> is already in its <span class="ltx_text ltx_markedasmath ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>, so double spending is prevented and FPAT-Safety is guaranteed. The full proof is presented in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx7" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Example.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ Example. ‣ 5 PaxPay Protocol ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> depicts a transfer:</p>
<ol id="S5.I7" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S5.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S5.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Alice wants to pay <math id="S5.I7.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline"><mn>3</mn></math> recipients with <math id="S5.I7.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline"><mn>2</mn></math> coins.
She generates 3 blinded coins and a matching NIZK, and sends them to the validators.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S5.I7.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Each validator checks the validity of the NIZK and that the old coins are not in its <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>, and, if so, sign the blinded coins and add the serial numbers to their <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">snList</span>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I7.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S5.I7.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Alice receives the signatures.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I7.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S5.I7.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">For each coin: once <math id="S5.I7.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> blinded partial signatures are received, Alice unblinds and then aggregates them into one aggregated signature.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S5.I7.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S5.I7.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Alice sends the coin tuples and their signatures to their recipients.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="fig/paxpay.png" id="S5.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" width="333" height="272" alt="Refer to caption"   style="width: 666px; height: unset; max-width: 100%">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">PaxPay example: Alice pays <math id="S5.F1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline"><mn>3</mn></math> recipients with <math id="S5.F1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline"><mn>2</mn></math> old coins.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Regulatory enforcement</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">PaxPay is designed as a private payment system.
As in PEReDi <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, PRCash <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> or Platypus <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, the protocol can be enhanced to be <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">regulation-compiant</em>.
The use of succinct proofs limits the impact of regulatory enforcement on the system’s performance.
This section describes how to build such a regulatory enforcement on top of the protocol described above.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Our regulatory enforcement is achieved via <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">compliance coins</em>.
Each user owns its unique compliance coin.
The coin commits to some data related to the user and all his transactions.
The user must attach the compliance coin to each of it transactions as an input and the validators will sign the updated compliance coin.
Well-formedness of the updated compliance coin is proved through NIZK.
As for a classical coin, the old compliance coin is spent by revealing its serial number.
As a result, a user has one one valid compliance coin at a time and this coin acts as an append-only tracing mechanism.
We introduce the following regulation features, shown in Table <a href="#S1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Summary. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>:</p>
<ul id="S6.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Limited held amount per user:</span> Users cannot hold more than <math id="S6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{max}_{held}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Full asset tracing:</span> A trusted authority (centralized or decentralized) can reveal the content of transaction to trace back assets and users activities.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Limited spendable amount per tx:</span> Users cannot spend more than <math id="S6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{max}_{sent}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msubsup></math> in one transfer.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Limited spendable amount in total:</span> Users cannot spend more than <math id="S6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V^{max}_{total}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msubsup></math> in total.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sanctions:</span> Users in the sanction list cannot send or receive funds.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I1.i6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Provable transaction history:</span> A user can prove arbitrary statements about her transactions. For instance, reveal all of her transactions and prove that the revealed set is complete (no transactions are missing).</p>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
<p class="ltx_p">Our regulatory construction enforce <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Limited spendable amount per tx</span>, <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Limited spendable amount in total</span>, <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Sanction list</span> and <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Provable transaction history</span>.
<math id="S6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{sent}^{max}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msubsup></math>, <math id="S6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V_{total}^{max}" display="inline"><msubsup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msubsup></math> and <math id="S6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> are public parameters chosen and potentially updated by the regulator.
The sanction list <math id="S6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> is represented as a sorted Merkle tree, which allows efficient proof of non-membership.</p>
</div>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Compliance coin.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The compliance coin of a user <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> is defined as a tuple
<math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="cc_{u}=(apk,\rho,v,com)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> where:</p>
<ul id="S6.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S6.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I2.i1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="apk" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> is <math id="S6.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>’s sole public address</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I2.i2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline"><mi>ρ</mi></math> the coin seed, as for a normal coin</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I2.i3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline"><mi>v</mi></math> is the total amount of money sent so far by <math id="S6.I2.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math></p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S6.I2.i4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S6.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I2.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="com" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> is the commitment to the list of all the transfer done by <math id="S6.I2.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> so far. For each coin created, it commits the tuple <math id="S6.I2.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(apk,v)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> with <math id="S6.I2.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="apk" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> the public key of the receiver and <math id="S6.I2.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline"><mi>v</mi></math> the value sent. It uses the incremental commitment introduced in Section <a href="#S3.SS3" title="3.3 Cryptographic tools ‣ 3 Model ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a></p>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="com" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> allows to trace <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>’s activities and allows <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> to prove additional statements on her transaction history in case of an update of the regulation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Registration.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Adding a user registration process is essential for regulatory enforcement, to comply with the <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">know-your-customer</em> (KYC) and <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">customer-due-diligence</em> (CDD) checks.
Additionally, it ensures the uniqueness of the compliance coin for each physical user.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">To this end, the validator storage is provided with a new list <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{registeredList}" display="inline"><mi>𝗋𝖾𝗀𝗂𝗌𝗍𝖾𝗋𝖾𝖽𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math>, the list of the enrolled users associated with their public key. <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{registeredList}" display="inline"><mi>𝗋𝖾𝗀𝗂𝗌𝗍𝖾𝗋𝖾𝖽𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math> is used to make sure that a physical user can only register once on the system.
The registration process is as follows for the user <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>:</p>
<ol id="S6.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S6.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Generate a random <math id="S6.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline"><mi>ρ</mi></math> and computes <math id="S6.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="cc_{u}=(apk_{u},\rho,0,0)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> and its blinding <math id="S6.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{cc}_{u}" display="inline"><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub></math> (with blinding factor <math id="S6.I3.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline"><mi>b</mi></math>).</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Computes an NIZK <math id="S6.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{register}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> that takes (<math id="S6.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{cc}_{u}" display="inline"><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub></math>, <math id="S6.I3.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="apk_{u}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math>) as public input and (<math id="S6.I3.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ask_{u},cc_{u},b" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math>) as private input. It proves that:</p>
<ol id="S6.I3.i2.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{cc}_{u}=\mathsf{BLIND}((apk_{u},\rho,0,0),b)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖡𝖫𝖨𝖭𝖣</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="ask_{u}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math> and <math id="S6.I3.i2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="apk_{u}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math> form a correct secret/public address pair.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Send to each validator <math id="S6.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{register}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math id="S6.I3.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\tilde{cc}_{u},apk_{u})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Upon correct KYC and CDD proving <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>’s identity, each validator check if <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{register}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>g</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> is correct and that: <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,*)\notin\mathsf{registeredList}" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∉</mo><mi>𝗋𝖾𝗀𝗂𝗌𝗍𝖾𝗋𝖾𝖽𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></mrow></math> (<math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> has registered no public address yet). If so, they sign <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{cc}_{u}" display="inline"><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>u</mi></msub></math>, send it back to <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>, and add <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u,apk_{u})" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> to <math id="S6.I3.i4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{registeredList}" display="inline"><mi>𝗋𝖾𝗀𝗂𝗌𝗍𝖾𝗋𝖾𝖽𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S6.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S6.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Once <math id="S6.I3.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> has received <math id="S6.I3.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2f+1" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> partial signature, she can unblind and aggregates the partial signatures to form a valid signature for <math id="S6.I3.i5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="cc_{u}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
</ol>
<p class="ltx_p">The detailed algorithm is described in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Transfer.</h4>

<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Section <a href="#S5" title="5 PaxPay Protocol ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> described how a transfer is handled by a user <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>, by spending <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline"><mi>n</mi></math> old coins <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{.75,0,.25}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{.75,0,.25}%
\mathbf{c}^{old}_{i}}]_{i=1}^{n}" display="inline"><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">𝐜</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">i</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#BF0040;" mathcolor="#BF0040">d</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></math>
and creating <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m+1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> new coins <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}\tilde{%

<p class="ltx_p">Conditions (1) ensures that all the input coins belong to the owner of the input compliance coin.
Condition (2) ensures that <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>, the user that invokes <em class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">transfer</em>, is the owner of the compliance coin. Condition (3) ensures that the redeem coin will belong to <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math>.
Conditions (4), (5), (6) and (7) ensure that the new compliance coin is well-formed.
Condition (8), (9) and (10) ensure that the transfer is compliant. (8) verifies that the amount of the transfer does not exceed that maximum allowed for a single transfer.
(9) verifies that the total amount of money sent by <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline"><mi>u</mi></math> does not exceed that maximum amount.
(10) verifies that the sender is not a user under sanctions.
(11) verifies that none of the receivers of the transfer is under sanction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The user storage is also augmented with a list <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{comList}" display="inline"><mi>𝖼𝗈𝗆𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math>, in which she stores the tuples <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(apk,v,r)" display="inline"><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> that she has used at each transfer.
At the end of the transfer described above, she thus append to <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{comList}" display="inline"><mi>𝖼𝗈𝗆𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math> the following: <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\forall j,j\in[1,m],({\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{pgfstrokecolor}{%
rgb}{0,0,1}apk^{new}_{j}},{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}\definecolor[named]{%
pgfstrokecolor}{rgb}{0,0,1}v^{new}_{j}},r_{j})" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∀</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">k</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">v</mi><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">j</mi><mrow><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi style="--ltx-fg-color:#0000FF;" mathcolor="#0000FF">w</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.
She can later use <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{comList}" display="inline"><mi>𝖼𝗈𝗆𝖫𝗂𝗌𝗍</mi></math> and her compliance coin to prove any statement about her transaction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Upon receiving correct proofs (<math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{comply},\pi_{transfer}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></math>) and their public parameters, the validators execute the same algorithm as for a non regulated transfer, except that they verify both <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{comply}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math id="S6.SS0.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{transfer}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math>. They can then sign the news coins and then send the signature back.
The detailed algorithm is described in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>PaxPay implementation and performance</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">PaxPay implementation in Golang is available on Github.
We developed with two implementations, with and without regulation support.
Below we overview the cryptographic tools we employed and report on the performance of our protocols.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.1 </span>Cryptographic building blocks</h3>

<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">NIZK.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">NIZK proofs are implemented using the Groth16 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite> protocol.
Groth16 allows for constructing succinct non-interactive arguments of knowledge (SNARKs) with constant verification complexity, regardless of the complexity of the relation <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></math> it attests to. The relation <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}" display="inline"><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi></math> is represented by an arithmetic circuit.
We instantiate this scheme with the BW6-761 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> curve, designed to cycle with the BL12-377 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> curve, allowing for efficient pairing verification over BL12-377 within the SNARK.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">In the regulated version, each transfer requires two NIZK. For performance reasons, these two proofs <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{transfer}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>f</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>e</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{comply}" display="inline"><msub><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math> are merged into a single proof with a unique circuit.
The proof of non-membership in the merkle tree is implemented as follows: the sanction list has the following form: <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList=[s_{1},s_{2},...,s_{\xi}]" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>ξ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></math>. <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math> is supposed to be published sorted by the regulator.
To verify the non-inclusion of an address <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="apk" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></math> in the list, we prove that there exist <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math> such that:</p>
<ul id="S7.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S7.I1.i1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math> are elements of <math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>.</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S7.I1.i2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j=i+1" display="inline"><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow></math> (<math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></math> and <math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{j}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></math> are consecutive elements of <math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SancList" display="inline"><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></math>).</p>
</div>
</li>
<li id="S7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><math id="S7.I1.i3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\blacksquare" display="inline"><mi mathvariant="normal">■</mi></math></span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{i}<apk<s_{j}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo><</mo><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo><</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></math> (<math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{1}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s_{\xi}" display="inline"><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>ξ</mi></msub></math> are set to <math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0x00..00" display="inline"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>⁢</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mn>00..00</mn></mrow></math> and <math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="0xFF..FF" display="inline"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mi>x</mi><mi>F</mi><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">.</mo><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mi>F</mi><mi>F</mi></mrow></math> to make sure this constraint can always be fulfilled).</p>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Hash functions and <span class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">PRF</span>.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">To optimize the computational cost of the proving algorithm in SNARK, we rely on MiMC <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite>.
MiMC is an arithmetization-oriented, collision-resistant and preimage-resistant hash function that is efficiently represented as arithmetic circuits. We use it to derive the the seeds <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline"><mi>ρ</mi></math> of created coins from the serial numbers <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="sn" display="inline"><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> of spent coins.
The pseudorandom function family <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{PRF}_{x}()" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>𝖯𝖱𝖥</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is derived from a MiMC function <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}" display="inline"><mi>𝖧</mi></math> as <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathsf{PRF}_{x}(m):=\mathsf{H}(m||x)" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>𝖯𝖱𝖥</mi><mi>x</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mi>𝖧</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>.<span id="footnote7" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">7</sup><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">7</span>The natural way to implement a <math id="footnote7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{PRF}" display="inline"><mi>𝖯𝖱𝖥</mi></math> from a hash function is to consider <math id="footnote7.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathsf{PRF_{x}:=H(m||x)}" display="inline"><mrow><msub><mi>𝖯𝖱𝖥</mi><mi>𝗑</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mi>𝖧</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝗆</mi><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>𝗑</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math>, however, replacing concatenation by an addition in the field does not compromise security in our case while reducing the computational cost.</span></span></span></p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">Incremental commitment scheme.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">The incremental commitment scheme is also derived from the MiMC function <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{H}" display="inline"><mi>𝖧</mi></math>. Given a commitment <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="com^{old}" display="inline"><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></math> and a message <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m" display="inline"><mi>m</mi></math> to be added to the commitment with a randomness <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline"><mi>r</mi></math>, <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{INCR}(com^{old},m,r)" display="inline"><mrow><mi>𝖨𝖭𝖢𝖱</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></math> is defined as follows: <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{INCR}(com^{old},m,r)=\mathsf{H}(com^{old}||m||r)" display="inline"><mrow><mrow><mi>𝖨𝖭𝖢𝖱</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖧</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>⁢</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>⁢</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>m</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mo>⁢</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></math>. The commitment function <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{COM}" display="inline"><mi>𝖢𝖮𝖬</mi></math> is then an iteration of increments <math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{INCR}" display="inline"><mi>𝖨𝖭𝖢𝖱</mi></math> over the sequence of messages and randomnesses provided.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx4" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">
<math id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{(k,N)}" display="inline"><mrow><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐤</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">,</mo><mi>𝐍</mi><mo class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math>-threshold blind signature.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS1.SSS0.P0.SPx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">Our signature scheme is based on a slightly modified version of the Coconut scheme <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, which itself is a variant of the Pointcheval and Sanders signature scheme <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>.
Indeed, certain checks originally performed using a sigma protocol in Coconut are instead handled in the Groth16 proof in our implementation, reducing the overall verification complexity. We instantiate this scheme with the BLS12-377 curve so that the verification algorithm, which involves pairings, is efficient in the Groth16 proof. More details about the construction are given in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">
<span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">7.2 </span>Performance analysis</h3>

<div id="S7.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We now report on our comparative performance analysis.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1" class="ltx_subparagraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subparagraph">NIZK Benchmark.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">We benchmarked our NIZK, implemented using a Groth16 SNARK, on an Intel i7 @ 2.6 GHz CPU running Ubuntu 22.04.
The results are summarized in Table <a href="#S7.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ NIZK Benchmark. ‣ 7.2 Performance analysis ‣ 7 PaxPay implementation and performance ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
Each value is based on the average of <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10" display="inline"><mn>10</mn></math> proving and verification runs.
A comparison with related protocols is provided in Table <a href="#S1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Summary. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.
The data in this table was gathered from the respective research papers, as the source codes of these protocols were not always publicly available.
However, the CPU used for our benchmark has comparable performance to the machines reported in those works: they all use Intel Core i7 CPUs except for Zef and UTT.
For Zef and UTT, AWS EC2 instances were used for the benchmark. These two types of instance have similar CPUs (Intel Xeon Platinum 8175 and 8124).</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">PaxPay has two implementations: with and without the regulatory feature.
The benchmark was conducted on both.
The regulated version, running on a single core, serves as a reference point.
The results indicate that our SNARK verification time is notably short, taking only <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5.6" display="inline"><mn>5.6</mn></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> ms</span>.
As shown in Table <a href="#S1.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Summary. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, this verification time is between <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="8" display="inline"><mn>8</mn></math> and <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="100" display="inline"><mn>100</mn></math> times shorter than the NIZK verification times reported in other works (except for Zcash, which takes approximately the same time but suffers from other major issues discussed in Section <a href="#S8" title="8 Discussion and comparison with related protocols ‣ Fast, Private and Regulated Payments in Asynchronous Networks" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>).
The verification time is a key metric since slow verification limits the transaction throughput of the system.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p class="ltx_p">This fast verification comes at the cost of relatively slow proving, requiring nearly <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="7" display="inline"><mn>7</mn></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> s</span> to generate a proof for a transfer on a single core. However, with <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline"><mn>6</mn></math> cores, the proving time drops to <math id="S7.SS2.SSS0.P0.SPx1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline"><mn>2</mn></math><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> s</span>.</p>
</div>
